evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'It fails in CI. Now it fails on your laptop too.' plus bolded lede 'Rerun is a free command-line tool for backend engineers' that says it records in CI and replays locally. The install card beside it ('Copy install command') gives the next step. Nothing later muddies it.
evidence.fit: Answers 'devs want to see it work' with an operable replay directly under the hero. Handles the no-logos fact plainly in the pricing section ('There are GitHub stars and no customer logos, so the proof on this page is the replay above and the source'). Says 'hosted team version is planned, not built'. Docs and GitHub URLs are used as the brief supplied them. The 'What a replay cannot do yet' section suits a sceptical engineer, though it adds scope facts (Node-only) the brief did not state.
evidence.distinctiveness: The twin-track 'tape' (CI-recorded column against a laptop column, with a toggle between 'rerun replay ci-8841' and 'npm test (no rerun)') is a product-specific artifact: it shows the counterfactual, not just a terminal. The rest is a familiar dev-tool kit: hero with install card, 2x2 grid of mechanism cards, steps beside a dark code block, $0 pricing card, CTA band. System Helvetica/Inter fallbacks and a stock blue accent read as competent rather than ownable.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the tape's controls and the first three event rows sit inside the first viewport. It loads in the completed 'FAIL · reproduced' state. Switching to 'npm test (no rerun)' gives 'PASS · not reproduced' with 6 of 7 rows marked 'differs' in red. That answers the core doubt: why does it pass locally? The coupon/midnight story matches the terminal block further down ('Expected: 80 Received: 100'), and that block says 'The sample above is the same run the tape at the top replays'. Docked from 9 because at 390 the tape begins at y=734 and its Replay button sits at y=1296, in the second screen.
evidence.craft: Clear type scale (64px H1, 22px lede, 26px section heads), token-based spacing and a consistent hairline-rule system. Status colours (red 'differs', green 'same', blue head-row bar) are used with meaning. The 1440 hero leaves a balanced right column for the install card. Minor issues: the tape-head H2 and its paragraph sit on one awkward baseline row at 1440, and the 13px row notes inside the table are small. No overlaps or clipping at 1440, 768 or 390 in any state I put the tape into.
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed rather than shrunk. The table header is hidden, each event becomes a card with 'CI run' and 'Laptop' labels, and the outcome badge is reordered above the controls. Mode buttons, Replay and the slider are all 44px tall. The 'Menu' details button opens a dropdown and closes once a link is chosen (I tapped 'Limits'; menu closed and the page scrolled). No overflow at 390 or 320. Costs: the artifact only starts at y=734, so the first screen is headline plus install card; inline text links ('Read the docs', footer links) are 17–20px tall.
evidence.honesty: 'Sample recording written for this page. It runs in your browser; nothing is installed, fetched or sent.' sits directly under the tape at every width. The code block says 'Example. Exact flags are in the docs.' and 'Command names and output are illustrative'. The primary action is 'Copy install command', which copies exactly the npm command shown. Planned hosted version: 'Not built yet; no date to announce.' No invented users or metrics.
evidence.interaction: At 1440, 768 and 390 I ran every tape state. 'Replay the run' runs RUNNING, then FAIL · reproduced; pressing it mid-run turns it into Stop, which leaves 'STOPPED AT 1/7'. Dragging the slider to 3 gives 'STOPPED AT 3/7', and to 0 gives 'READY' with instructions. Switching mode re-renders both columns and the badge. Arrow keys move between the mode radios. Copy wrote 'npm install -g @rerun/cli' to the clipboard, and 'Copied: npm install -g @rerun/cli' appeared right under the button. Both copy buttons have a written fallback message. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific nouns from the engineer's world: 'setTimeout(1200) that crossed midnight in CI crosses midnight again on your laptop at two in the afternoon', 'Treat a .rerun file the way you treat a log file'. Each button says what it does ('Copy install command', 'Replay the run', 'View the source on GitHub'). Outcome microcopy is written, not defaulted. Small redundancy: 'Free and MIT-licensed' appears in four places.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, named audience ('for backend engineers'), copy action and the top of the operable tape showing matched CI and laptop values are all in one viewport. 390: promise, lede and install card fill the viewport, and only the tape's H2 peeks in at the bottom. So the believable proof is not in view on the phone.

problems: At 390 the replay artifact begins below the first screen (tape top y=734, Replay button y=1296), so the phone's first viewport makes the promise without the proof

The section system after the tape is the familiar dev-tool template (2x2 cards, steps plus dark code block, $0 card, CTA band), and the type is system fallbacks with a stock blue, so the page is recognisable by its artifact only

evidence.clarity: H1 'The test that only fails in CI, failing on your laptop.' and a lede on record and replay, 'Free, MIT-licensed, one command to install', followed by the install command and Copy. Clear, but the audience is implied rather than named, and the participial headline takes a second read.
evidence.fit: The tone is right for distrustful engineers: a serif editorial voice, and 'You would normally find a row of company logos here. We don't have company users we can name yet'. 'Hosted team version ... planned but not built; there is no waitlist' resolves the planned-version tension. But it fills the gap with facts the brief did not supply: 'Two people, part time', reply SLAs, a supported-CI matrix, '2–4% ... in our measurements', 'issues from people running it in real pipelines'. That undercuts the honest framing.
evidence.distinctiveness: Charter-style serif body and headlines against a mono terminal is a real point of view in a category of sans dev-tool pages, and the red recording dot carries from wordmark to terminal to scrubber. The artifact, though, is the standard 'animated terminal in the hero' dev-tool trope, and the remaining sections (steps, table, status list, FAQ accordion) are conventional.
evidence.proof: The terminal autoplays when it scrolls into view and runs the replay to '2 passing · 1 failing · identical to CI run 4821' and 'rerun diff ... 0 differ'. It is operable early. It only shows Rerun's own output, though, with no contrast against a plain local run, so it asserts reproduction rather than demonstrating it. Internal inconsistency: the note says 'The red tick is where the test fails, 2,003 ms in', but the tick sits at 0:05.6 of a 0:08.8 timeline. The sample is not labelled as an example (see honesty).
evidence.craft: Good serif type and a generous measure. At 1440 the hero is a narrow left column with the right half empty (h1 capped at 17ch inside a 1040px wrap). On load the terminal is a 420px-min-height black slab with three lines in it: the 1440 first screen and the operator's 1440.png both show a mostly empty terminal. The player controls (Play 76x25, speed 38x25) are cramped 13px mono buttons under the large terminal. Section rhythm is otherwise even.
evidence.mobile: 390: no page overflow and the three nav links fit inline. But the terminal's key lines are cut at the right edge and need sideways scrolling inside the terminal ('github-actions · run', 'refunds within the return window (2,003', 'identical to CI ru'). The very line that proves reproduction is truncated (screen scrollWidth 560 vs clientWidth 358). Play and speed controls are 25px tall, under 44. The terminal is 582px tall and starts at y=537, so most of it falls below the first screen.
evidence.honesty: Under the terminal: 'This is a recording of a real replay session, played back in the page.' The session (ci-8f3a2c, run 4821, api.stripe.test) is not in the brief, so a sample is presented as real. The FAQ states performance figures as measured fact: 'roughly 2–4% on the test run itself, in our measurements on Jest suites between 500 and 5,000 tests'. It also asserts 'Two people, part time. Issues get a reply within a few days', 'A typical recording ... is 1–5 MB' and 'issues from people running it in real pipelines'. The candid 'no logos' section is good, but it sits next to invented specifics.
evidence.interaction: At all three widths: autoplay ran to 0:08.8 and the button became 'Replay'. Dragging the scrubber to 5700 rendered 12 lines at 0:05.7. Speed cycles 1x/2x/4x, Play and Pause toggle, and Space on the focused terminal toggles playback. Copy changed to 'Copied' (green) and wrote the npm command to the clipboard. All six FAQ items open. No console errors. Feedback is thin outside the terminal: no reset, no state message beyond 'replaying/paused/done' in 13px grey, and the controls are small targets. Reduced motion jumps straight to the end state, which is sensible.
evidence.copy: Strong, specific lines: 'Three commands, start to breakpoint', 'Next time a test fails only in CI, replay it instead of staring at it', 'there is no waitlist because there is nothing to wait for yet'. The CTA button text is just 'Copy' (its aria-label is fuller). Credibility drops where copy states invented measurements as fact, and 'replays it exactly where you can put a breakpoint in it' is slightly tangled.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, lede, install and Copy are in view, but the terminal shows only 3 lines on load (autoplay begins after a 500ms delay), so nothing in the viewport yet backs the promise. 390: promise and install are in view, and the terminal header plus 3 truncated lines appear at the bottom. The specific promise and action are present, but the believable proof is not.

At 390 the terminal truncates its key lines ('identical to CI ru...', '(2,003'), so they need sideways scrolling inside the terminal, and the player controls are 25px tall

The first screen at 1440 is a narrow text column with empty right half plus a mostly empty black terminal on load. The artifact shows only Rerun's output, with no 'without Rerun' contrast, and its 2,003 ms tick note contradicts the 5.6 s tick position

hard_fail_flags.evidence: FAQ answer under 'How much does recording slow down CI?' states a performance number as measured fact: 'A few hundred milliseconds of startup, and roughly 2–4% on the test run itself, in our measurements on Jest suites between 500 and 5,000 tests. Numbers and the benchmark script are in the repository.' The brief supplies no performance figures. Separately, the note under the hero terminal presents the sample session as genuine: 'This is a recording of a real replay session, played back in the page.'
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P004/B/index.html from disk at 1440x900. Scroll to 'Questions engineers ask first' and click 'How much does recording slow down CI?' to read the 2–4% claim. The 'real replay session' sentence is the grey paragraph directly below the hero terminal.

reason: A's twin-track tape is the better product artifact. It shows the same run passing without Rerun and failing with it, it is operable in the first 1440 screen, it is labelled as a sample right where it appears, and it holds up at every width. B has the more ownable typography and a likeable voice, but it presents an invented session as 'real', asserts measured performance numbers, and truncates its proof lines on the phone. A would lose only if its sections below the tape were judged too templated to ship, and that does not outweigh B's honesty and mobile problems.
